name: White Clover

facts.how: Flowers raw or as tea; leaves cooked

caution: Eat clover in modest amounts and best cooked or dried for tea, since large quantities of raw clover can cause bloating. Harvest from unsprayed lawns. Never eat a wild plant on this guide's word alone. Confirm identity against several sources and learn the look-alikes first.

sections.title: Identification
sections.body: The familiar three-leaflet lawn clover with round white flower heads. Truly abundant and easy to know.

sections.title: Uses
sections.body: The sweet flower heads make a pleasant nibble and a mild tea; young leaves are best lightly cooked.
